title: Ang 664–690: the Gurus in Dhanasri
hook: whatever you ask of your Master, on ang 681
tomorrow: if what you're after is close, why go searching the forest?

segments.voice: That was the week: longer hymns, the ballad, the bhagats, medicine, Dhanasri, and last night, the sky's aarti, with a light in everyone. Today the Gurus fill the rest of Dhanasri.
screen: `THE SKY'S AARTI.` → `LONGER HYMNS, THE BALLAD, THE BHAGATS, MEDICINE.`

segments.voice: Birthday lists, wish lists, the cart full of things you'll never check out. Asking comes easily when the asking is for stuff. Yesterday's question was harder: if you could ask for anything, what would it be? On ang 681, Guru Arjan says something that sounds like a blank check. Whatever I ask of my Master, he gives me.
screen: `THE CART YOU NEVER CHECK OUT.` → `ANYTHING AT ALL?` → `WHATEVER I ASK, HE GIVES.`

segments.voice: These pages hold the Gurus' hymns in Dhanasri, in order: Guru Amar Das, Guru Ram Das, then Guru Arjan. And here's his line, in paraphrase: whatever I ask of my Lord and Master, he gives me; whatever his servant Nanak says comes true, here and hereafter. Now look at who is speaking. Not a customer. A servant, a daas, someone whose life is already turned toward the Master. That changes the asking. The line isn't a promise that any wish list gets filled. It's what trust sounds like between a servant and the one he serves: the asking comes out of the relationship, so it already leans toward what the Master would give. It's the same turn Dhanasri made at its start: fear brought to the Giver, now asking brought to the Master. So the question isn't only what you'd ask for. It's who you'd be by the time you asked, and whether you'd trust the answer if it came back different.
screen: `THREE GURUS IN DHANASRI.` · `WHATEVER I ASK, HE GIVES.` · `SPOKEN BY A SERVANT.` · then, large: `ASK.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and sit still. Let one honest ask come up, whatever it is, without judging it. Then hold it quietly for the rest of the sit, and notice whether it changes shape the longer you hold it.
Ang 664. Where the Gurus' hymns in Dhanasri begin, leading to Guru Arjan's line: whatever I ask of my Master, he gives.
Your line: ask, the way a servant asks a Master he trusts. Two weeks, a whole wedding, done.
